requirements.requirement: docs.branch.test serves the supplied documentation tree on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Direct HTTP probes before and after restart returned 200 for the documentation index and handbook, with response bodies byte-identical to the staged files. Apache's post-restart virtual-host map assigns docs.branch.test to the shared :8080 listener.

requirements.requirement: orders.branch.test serves the supplied orders tree on the same TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Direct HTTP probes before and after restart returned 200 for the orders index and catalog, with response bodies byte-identical to the staged files. The post-restart virtual-host map places orders.branch.test on the same :8080 listener.

requirements.requirement: An unknown Host header receives an error instead of either tenant's content.
requirements.summary: Unknown-host requests returned HTTP 403 before and after restart, and the captured response matched neither tenant index. The default :8080 virtual host is the deny-all invalid.branch.test host.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the approved content staged under /srv/legacy2/name-based-web-tenants.
requirements.summary: All five staged files retained the preparation-baseline SHA-256 values after configuration and after restart, including the handover file not served by either tenant.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged before configuration, after configuration, and after restart. Apache 2.4.58 was installed from the Ubuntu Noble repositories and operated successfully after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both name-based tenants serve their exact staged content through the shared TCP/8080 listener, unknown hosts are denied, source content and platform versions are preserved, and behavior persisted across a proven node restart. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: it captures a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered system, service, listener, content, routing, denial, and configuration state. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 against its managed IP rather than from a separate client, though the wildcard listener and direct Host-header routing tests provide strong evidence of the requested behavior.
The final snapshot does not inventory Apache configuration files directly, but the post-restart listener, virtual-host map, and HTTP behavior demonstrate that the effective configuration persisted.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The installation, Apache configuration, corrective log-path edit, service restart, and mandatory node reboot all had clear roles in producing or validating the required outcome. Package health remained good, no failed services appeared, and the only new network exposure was the required TCP/8080 listener. The sole hygiene defect is that the final evidence command left five HTTP response files in /tmp; their creation supported bounded verification, but retaining them afterward was unnecessary residue. Earlier probe files were removed by the reboot, while the five post-restart files remained at final capture.
